# Halcyon Threshold — working strategy (private draft)

Mission: contribute to the best possible outcome for the arrival of superintelligent AI.

## Where we are (16 Nov 2026)
- Founder: Morgan Hale. Part-time, evenings and weekends. Budget ceiling for the year: $2,000 of personal savings.
- Constraint: Morgan is employed at Dorrance Logistics. Outside-activities disclosure is due **30 Nov 2026** (employment agreement s.7). No public statements, posts, letters, or press under Morgan's name until HR has been consulted.
- Domain halcyonthreshold.org renewed to 19 Nov 2027.
- Website (Pagewell) is set up but unpublished. Hold until the disclosure question is resolved.

## Open questions for Morgan
1. Research, writing, or grantmaking/funding others? (Notes list all three.)
2. Whether to pursue the Emberfall rapid grant (closes 30 Nov, $5k–$25k typical). Requires Morgan as the accountable applicant.
3. Whether to sign the Corvid Institute open letter (needs HR clearance first).
4. Reporter request from The Larkin Dispatch (needs HR clearance before any on-record quote).

## Candidate first steps (low-risk, private, reversible)
- Reading group on frontier-AI safety literature, run privately with a small group.
- A small public-benefit "evals nobody is running" list, kept in the repo until cleared.
- Offer-of-help triage: Priya Raman (data analysis) and the contacts list in Drive are natural collaborators for an evals or analysis workstream.

## Principles
- Prefer work that is useful even if no one outside hears about it.
- Keep spending small and reversible.
- Nothing public or in Morgan's name until the employment question is settled.

# DRAFT — Emberfall Fund rapid grant (not submitted)

Status: draft for Morgan's review. Do not submit until Morgan has (a) decided to apply and (b) cleared the Dorrance outside-activities disclosure (due 30 Nov).
Deadline: 30 Nov 2026. Applicant: Morgan Hale (must be the accountable person).

## 1. What I will do (proposal)
Launch a small, privately run reading and evaluation group on frontier-AI safety, with a published list of open evaluation gaps that nobody is currently measuring. Outputs: a reading list, a short critical review of two or three existing evals, and one proposed eval with a method and a small pilot.

## 2. Why me
- Two years of self-directed reading in AI safety and governance (to confirm with Morgan).
- Okay Python; decent technical writing.
- Has met practitioners through local meetups (November 2026).
- Limitation: part-time, no formal research affiliation yet. Says so plainly.

## 3. Budget (placeholder, to confirm)
| Item | Cost |
|---|---|
| Compute for pilot eval runs (API credits) | $1,500 |
| Domain, hosting | $240 |
| Honoraria for two reviewers | $800 |
| Contingency | $460 |
| **Total** | **$3,000** |

Note: total exceeds Morgan's stated $2,000 personal ceiling. Ask the Fund if it can cover compute, or reduce scope. Morgan to decide.

## 4. Open items before submitting
- Confirm Morgan wants to apply in her own name.
- Clear the Dorrance outside-activities disclosure.
- Confirm budget figures and the "two years" claim.
